title: How Stroppy Cloud works
lead: What a benchmark is made of, what happens at launch and where each part runs — your data and machines stay in your cloud.

model.title: What you work with
model.sub: A database and a workload make a test; a test, a suite or a schedule launches a run; a run leaves a result.

arch.title: Architecture
arch.sub: What it is made of and what goes between the parts. Hover a block to see how it works.

console.title: Console
console.more: A single-page app. Everything comes from the Stroppy Cloud server: REST for data, one WebSocket for a live run — logs, metrics and progress without reloading.

api.title: Server
api.more: The product server and the only door out: tenants and roles, the library, compiling a test into a fully resolved RunSpec, quotas, launching in Graphene, projecting a live run, rating, compare, public reports.

identity.title: Accounts
identity.more: Sign up, sign in, e-mail confirmation and recovery by code. A session becomes a short-lived JWT; the server checks its signature itself, with no call per request.

state.title: Server database
state.more: Everything created in the console, the index and results of runs. Cloud keys never land here: they go as secrets into the tenant's namespace in Graphene.

pipes.title: Pipelines
pipes.more: The run is plain Go: create the network and machines, lay out containers, drive the load segments, collect the result. Built into one image with the server; on start the server publishes the binaries and manifests into every tenant's namespace.

door.title: Graphene server
door.more: One port for all: management (Connect), workers and agents (gRPC), the image registry (/v2), telemetry intake (OTLP). Checks namespace access and drives runs.

temporal.title: Temporal
temporal.more: A run is a workflow and every resource (machine, container, artifact, stand) a long-lived record with an owner. Hence guaranteed teardown: children die before parents, and a worker crash does not lose the run.

registry.title: Registry
registry.more: Holds pipeline worker images; blobs are deduplicated by digest, so publishing to a new tenant is only a manifest.

worker.title: Run worker
worker.more: At run start Graphene brings up a container with the pipeline image; it drives the workflow through its phases and stops once the run is over and its records are gone.

crossplane.title: Provisioning
crossplane.more: Machines and networks are declared as Kubernetes resources; Crossplane creates them in your account through the tenant's ProviderConfig built from its secret, and removes them with the run.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.more: Everything a run writes about itself, over standard protocols. The Stroppy server reads it through the Graphene door with the tenant's rights — store addresses never leave.

agent.title: Agent
agent.more: Installed by cloud-init, it keeps its own outgoing gRPC session to Graphene (opens no ports), starts the run's containers and ships their telemetry.

db.title: Database
db.more: The chosen DBMS and topology — nodes, replicas, proxies — as docker images on the stand's machines. They live only for the run unless the stand is kept.

runner.title: Runner
runner.more: A separate machine with stroppy: loads the data and drives the scenario in segments; metrics leave through the agent.

all.title: The whole
all.body: Four zones: your browser, the Stroppy Cloud product server, the Graphene execution core, and your cloud, where the stand lives.

launch.title: Launch
launch.body: The console asks the server to launch a test. The server checks rights and quotas, compiles the test into a RunSpec and starts a run in Graphene — which records it as a workflow in Temporal.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.body: Graphene brings up a worker with the stroppy-run image from its registry. The Stroppy server put that image there itself at start — the pipeline version always equals the server's.

stand.title: Stand
stand.body: The worker declares the network and machines; Crossplane creates them in your account with the tenant's key. An agent comes up on every machine and connects to Graphene by itself.

run.title: Run
run.body: Agents start the database and runner containers; stroppy loads the data and drives the load segments.

observe.title: Observe
observe.body: Agents ship metrics and logs over OTLP. The server reads them through Graphene and streams them to the console over WebSocket — that is how a run is live.
